title: SSE client backpressure hints and reconnect negotiation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket specifies a server+client negotiation extension for Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections that allows clients to advertise backpressure capability and preferred reconnect semantics, and for the server to reply with negotiated window sizes, checkpointing hints, and an optional resumable token format. The goal is to reduce duplicate token replay and wasted compute after reconnects, allow low-latency clients to request smaller buffer windows, and maintain compatibility with our existing resume token protocol and legacy clients.

Background & motivations:
- Current SSE resume tokens in the platform are robust but coarse-grained: they assume the server will hold a contiguous window of N tokens for all connections. This leads to either high memory overhead (large N for safety) or frequent replayed work post-reconnect (small N).
- Customers running interactive apps over flaky mobile networks see higher perceived latency and cost when the platform replays multiple tokens. Some clients can apply backpressure (drop speculative in-progress streams or latch partial output) and prefer fine-grained checkpoints.
- We need a backward-compatible extension that enables flexible per-client window negotiation, explicit ack semantics from clients, and explicit fallbacks for legacy clients and proxies that strip custom headers.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Client Hello: on initial connect, the client MAY send an HTTP header X-RW-SSE-Client-Hints with a compact value describing: preferred_resume_window (tokens), ack_mode (none|counted|byte-aware), keepalive_interval_ms, and feature_flags (e.g., support_compact_tokens). The header is optional and must be ignored by legacy servers. Example header value: "w=16;ack=counted;ka=30000;flags=compact".

2) Server Hello (response headers): the server replies with X-RW-SSE-Server-Config indicating the negotiated window and recommended checkpoint frequency, e.g., "w=8;ckpt=64;token=compact-v2". If the server does not support the header, the client falls back to legacy resume behavior.

3) Inline control events: during the SSE stream, server emits a control event of type "rw-ckpt" with a base64 token string when it observes a natural checkpoint (e.g., model output boundary or token quota threshold). The event payload is a compact opaque string; clients must not parse internals but may store it and provide on reconnect. Example event: event: rw-ckpt
data: <base64-token>

4) Client ACKs: when client acknowledges receipt of a checkpoint, it can POST to a lightweight endpoint /sse/ack or send an inline event ack via a dedicated bidirectional channel where available. The ack informs the server it can advance its durable checkpoint window, enabling memory reclamation earlier for long tail connections.

5) Reconnect negotiation: on reconnect the client includes the last seen rw-ckpt token in the Last-Event-ID header or X-RW-Resume-Token. If token validation fails server returns HTTP 412 with a brief human-readable reason header X-RW-Resume-Reason and suggests fallback behavior (full resend or partial resend up to N tokens).

Compatibility & fallback rules:
- Legacy clients: omit X-RW headers; servers must behave exactly as today using existing resume semantics.
- Proxies that strip headers: control events are in-band SSE events (rw-ckpt) so they are resilient to header loss.
- Partial implementations: servers that only support server-side negotiation should still respond to X-RW-SSE-Client-Hints and emit rw-ckpt events even if acks are not consumed.

Operational behavior and observability:
- New metrics: sse.resume_attempts, sse.resume_success_rate, sse.replay_tokens_per_reconnect (histogram), sse.ack_latency_ms, sse.window_negotiated_distribution.
- Tracing: attach resume token id and negotiated window to traces for failed reconnects to surface where replay originated.
- Limits: cap negotiated windows per-customer with admin policy (e.g., max 128 tokens) to avoid DoS memory use.

Trade-offs considered:
- Header-based negotiation is compact but can be stripped by intermediaries; we thus duplicate important signals as in-band control events to preserve resumability.
- Allowing client acks to free server memory earlier increases complexity (new ack endpoint, auth scope) but reduces average memory footprint and cost for high-churn mobile customers.
- Byte-aware ack mode is more precise for very long tokens but harder to implement across heterogeneous model outputs; we recommend starting with counted-token ack_mode.

Security & privacy:
- Resume tokens are opaque and must be HMAC-signed with a server secret; clients never need to parse contents.
- Acks must be authenticated with the same token or API key used by the stream.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server responds with X-RW-SSE-Server-Config header when client hints are supplied and negotiated values are applied to that stream.
- Server emits rw-ckpt events at configured checkpoint intervals and tokens validate on reconnect.
- When a client sends last seen token on reconnect, server must either accept and resume from token (with <= negotiated window replay) or return 412 with a clear X-RW-Resume-Reason and recommended fallback.
- Metrics for replay tokens per reconnect and ack latency are available in the console.
- Backwards compatibility verified: legacy clients continue to resume using current behavior with no regressions.

Implementation plan (phased):
- Phase 1 (3 wks): header parsing + server-side negotiation + emit rw-ckpt events; record metrics; unit tests.
- Phase 2 (2 wks): ack endpoint and token expiry/memory reclamation; e2e with mobile client.
- Phase 3 (1 wk): rollout policy, admin caps per customer, console dashboard tiles.

Rollout & rollout policy:
- Canary: enable in staging with internal customers; opt-in gate controlled by feature flag per-customer.
- Gradual ramp after 2 weeks of metrics showing reduced replay tokens and no increase in failed resume rate.

Open questions / out-of-scope:
- Whether to use Last-Event-ID exclusively or a separate X-RW-Resume-Token header for tokens with embedded metadata. Proposal: support both but prefer X-RW-Resume-Token for opaque tokens that may include non-ASCII.
- Backpressure signaling from server to client to slow generation rate is out-of-scope for this ticket.

References & artifacts:
See related design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+client+negotiation and spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234
